title: Ombu: Giant Ombus You Can Visit
meta_description: Not wood. The ombu is a giant herb from the Argentine pampas whose trunk is soft water-storing tissue. Lisbon's largest is 10.9 metres round.
intro: The ombu is not wood at all. Phytolacca dioica is a giant herb that behaves like a tree, a soft stemmed relative of spinach whose swollen base is water storing tissue you could dent with a thumbnail, laid down for the dry seasons of the Argentine pampas it comes from. It grows fast and cannot be aged by counting rings, which is why the one in Cadiz is undated. What it does instead is get very wide. Two in a single Lisbon garden came out at 10.45 and 10.4 metres around, and the one at Largo do Limoeiro is wider than the house fronts on the street. Seville's is credited to seed that Christopher Columbus's son brought back around 1529. In Lima, the ombu at the Quinta de los Libertadores is said to have grown from seed José de San Martín carried up from Argentina in 1821.
